Implementation complete; recording two justified deviations from the certified plan before commit.

**1. Two test-body edits, against Scope's "out of scope: any test body change."**

The plan assumed renaming is purely a path operation. Three sites hold a renamed module as a *string literal*, which no import graph reveals and which AC6 (`make verify` green) forces:

- `tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py:29` — `_SIGNER_MODULES`, a pytest argv tuple.
- `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_bridge_vocabulary_stale.py:35,37` — `_WHOLE_FILE_ALLOWLIST`, which names *itself* and `test_bridge_vocabulary_e2e_heldout.py`.
- `scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt:17` — a path-keyed allowlist line (not a test body).

The first two are test-body edits. They change no assertion and no behaviour; they update a path literal so the test keeps testing what it tested before. Leaving them stale fails AC6, so the deviation is the narrower of the two options.

**2. `.test_durations` refreshed by key rewrite, not by re-capture.**

`file_impact` declared this file ("refresh durations capture after ~170 module node ids change across the epic"). Re-capturing via `pytest --store-durations` would have *dropped* every key outside `make test`'s selection (`not integration and not external`), because pytest-split rewrites the file with only the tests that ran. Instead the node-ID keys were rewritten in place from the rename map:

- 656 keys renamed for this story's 76 modules
- 887 keys remapped for earlier stories in this epic (S1–S4 renamed modules without refreshing durations)
- 5 dropped: 4 modules with no surviving counterpart, 1 colliding stale key
- 19,862 → 19,857 keys; `_heldout` keys remaining: **0**

Every duration value is preserved. The file round-trips byte-for-byte under `json.dumps(indent=4, sort_keys=True)` with no trailing newline, verified before editing, so the diff is 1542/1548 lines of real change rather than a whole-file reformat.

## Context / Problem
**76 held-out modules (13,930 LOC) have no base twin** (re-measured on origin/main 7927904a0 by listing every tracked `tests/**/*.py` and checking each `_heldout` module for a same-directory base). CORRECTED: this plan previously said 88, which is the count of *paired* held-out modules, not unpaired — the tree holds 164 held-out modules, 88 paired and 76 unpaired, and the two numbers were transposed. The 88 paired are exactly the ones S1-S4 merge (39 + 22 + 10 + 17), which is the cross-check that fixes the figure. 10 of them are handled elsewhere: the 8 `tests/scripts/*_seam_clean_heldout.py` modules and `tests/unit/reconciler/test_rich_text_seam_heldout.py` in the test-suite epic's seam story (E10a-S1) — re-measured on origin/main d74d53a5ffd, that story has LANDED and all 9 are already gone (only the base `tests/unit/reconciler/test_rich_text_seam.py` survives), so this carve-out is now a statement of completed work, not of pending work, and `tests/unit/test_config_gate_wiring_heldout.py`, deleted in its single-owner story (E10a-S3). The remaining 76 (unit 53, interfaces 18, scripts 4, integration 1) keep a `_heldout` suffix that no longer distinguishes anything once S2, S3 and S4 have merged every pair. Three of the 76 are cross-tier twins whose base lives in another directory and would collide on basename under pytest's prepend import mode (13 `__init__.py` files under `tests/`; no `--import-mode` in `pyproject.toml:8`), so they take a disambiguating suffix instead. The rename rules and the three cross-tier renames are itemised in this ticket's first comment. All counts and paths in this plan were re-measured on origin/main 7927904a0, and independently re-confirmed on origin/main ce5795c6a5c (2026-10-31): 164 held-out modules, 88 paired, 76 unpaired, tier split unit 53 / interfaces 18 / scripts 4 / integration 1, each derived by listing every tracked `tests/**/*.py` and testing each `_heldout` module for a same-directory base rather than by sampling.

## Approach
- `git mv` each of the **73** ordinary unpaired modules from `test_<name>_heldout.py` to `test_<name>.py`, in place, with no content change.
- The three cross-tier files take disambiguating suffixes: `tests/interfaces/store/test_repair_pause_ownership_heldout.py` (base `tests/scripts/graph/test_repair_pause_ownership.py`) → `test_repair_pause_ownership_store.py`; `tests/unit/reconciler/diffing/test_baseline_normalization_heldout.py` (base under `tests/integration/`) → `test_baseline_normalization_diffing.py`; `tests/unit/reconciler/test_identity_264f_heldout.py` (base `tests/unit/test_identity_264f.py`) → `test_identity_264f_reconciler.py`. Do not merge across tiers.
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_reconciler_last_pass_heldout.py` carries the tests E10a-S1 moved into it along with the rename.
- Paths are stated at their post-rename name: the reconciler epic (friended-brainsick-degus) rename has LANDED, so `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` no longer exists and the modules live under `tests/unit/reconciler/`.
- After this story `tests/**/test_*_heldout.py` matches nothing, and `git ls-files 'tests/*.py' | grep -v '__init__.py$' | grep -v 'conftest.py$' | xargs -n1 basename | sort | uniq -d` yields exactly `test_cli.py`, `test_link_sync.py`, `test_snapshot.py` — the same 3 as before this story; the epic's first acceptance criterion is checked here. NOTE: the unqualified duplicate-basename check is never empty on this tree — see the amended criterion below — so the epic's criterion is read as 'this story introduces no new duplicate basename'.

## Scope
In scope: the 76 unpaired `tests/**/test_*_heldout.py` modules (53 under `tests/unit/` including its subpackages, 18 under `tests/interfaces/`, 4 under `tests/scripts/`, 1 under `tests/integration/`), renamed in place. Out of scope: every merged pair (S1-S4), the 10 held-out modules handled by E10a-S1 and E10a-S3, module contents, every file under `src/`, and any test body change.

The 3 disambiguating suffixes are retained for clarity, not correctness. The stated rationale — a basename collision under pytest's prepend import mode — is not load-bearing: `tests/` carries only 13 `__init__.py` files and `pyproject.toml` sets no `--import-mode`, yet `test_cli.py`, `test_link_sync.py` and `test_snapshot.py` each already collide across directories today with the suite green. The suffixes still earn their place by keeping the 3 cross-tier modules distinguishable by name alone.


**Prerequisite figure reconciliation — this plan governs.** Prerequisites `19c3-0920` and `fb5f-54fd` each describe this story as "the 78 unpaired held-out renames (S5)", and 19c3 adds that it "claims the 55 unpaired modules under `tests/unit/` including its subpackages". Both figures are stale. `7a7a-ceb9` makes no such claim — the string "78 unpaired" occurs 0 times in its whole record. The 78 is not an independent count: it is the test-suite epic's enumeration arithmetic 88 - 10, quoted verbatim in this ticket's first comment, in which 88 is the **paired** count misread as unpaired. That is the transposition Context already records; correcting it gives 86 - 10 = 76, and 53 rather than 55 under `tests/unit/`. The 76 and the split 53/18/4/1 were re-derived by full enumeration on three `origin/main` SHAs (7927904a0, ce5795c6a5c, 757ca4852d7), never sampled. Where a prerequisite disagrees on these counts, this plan supersedes it.

## Testing
Per file: `pytest --collect-only -q <old path>` before and `pytest --collect-only -q <new path>` after — counts equal (recorded on this ticket as one table of 76 rows). `git ls-files 'tests/**/test_*_heldout.py'` prints nothing (it matches all 164 held-out modules today, so the glob is confirmed recursive); `git ls-files 'tests/*.py' | grep -v '__init__.py$' | grep -v 'conftest.py$' | xargs -n1 basename | sort | uniq -d` yields exactly `test_cli.py`, `test_link_sync.py`, `test_snapshot.py` — the same 3 as before this story; `make test` green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No `tests/**/test_*_heldout.py` file remains (`git ls-files 'tests/**/test_*_heldout.py'` prints nothing).
- [ ] The three cross-tier files carry their `_store`, `_diffing` and `_reconciler` suffixes.
- [ ] This story introduces **no new duplicate test-module basename**: `git ls-files 'tests/*.py' | grep -v '__init__.py$' | grep -v 'conftest.py$' | xargs -n1 basename | sort | uniq -d` yields exactly `test_cli.py`, `test_link_sync.py`, `test_snapshot.py` — the same 3 as before this story. AMENDED: this criterion previously required `git ls-files tests | xargs -n1 basename | sort | uniq -d` to print nothing, which is unreachable and unrelated to this story's work — on a clean tree it prints 10 lines (`__init__.py`, `conftest.py`, `README.md`, `pyproject.toml`, `code_arrow.json`, `prose.json`, `table.json`, plus the 3 pre-existing test-module collisions). Those duplicates are either intentional infrastructure or pre-date this story and sit outside its scope, so no correct implementation could satisfy the original wording. The before/after comparison is what this story actually controls.
- [ ] Node counts per file are unchanged across the rename, from the before/after `pytest --collect-only -q` table recorded on this ticket (76 rows).
- [ ] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` **exits 0**. AMENDED from `new=0`, which is unreachable: `new=N` counts marker-admitted entries, so an already-clean tree reports a nonzero `new` and still exits 0. Root cause: bug `6f24-3d47-b251-4905`, fixed in `AGENTS.md` and `rebar explain plan`.
- [ ] `make verify` green.
